physical: The more which-path information an interferometer records, the less visible its interference fringes; the two trade off so that distinguishability squared plus visibility squared is at most one.
reflected_sentence: The tradeoff between what can be distinguished and what can be seen keeps its shape.
rule_reason: Neither measure carries resistance and no qualifying cost or separation is supplied, so the rule says keeps. Distinguishability and visibility have no partners.
closing: The rule decides keeps because a tradeoff alone is not a resistance-caused limit. The sum must not be changed to a product, but neither operand has a frozen partner. The empty formula and interpretation avoid introducing substitutes or nonphysical numerical claims.
